title: Children's Online Safety Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to protect your child's privacy online. Covers parental controls, COPPA compliance, safe browsing, and screen time management.
intro: Protecting your child's privacy and safety online requires a comprehensive approach. This checklist covers essential steps every parent should take to create a secure digital environment for their children, from setting up parental controls to teaching safe browsing habits.

items.task: Install parental control software on all devices
items.why: Provides comprehensive monitoring and filtering across all your child's internet activities and helps enforce screen time limits.
items.howTo: Install trusted parental control software like Qustodio, Circle Home Plus, or Bark. Set up user profiles for each child with age-appropriate restrictions and monitoring levels.

items.task: Configure kid-safe browsers or browser restrictions
items.why: Prevents access to inappropriate content and limits exposure to tracking cookies and malicious websites.
items.howTo: Use browsers like Kiddle, KidzSearch, or configure a privacy-focused browser with strict content filters. Enable safe search on all search engines and block adult content.

items.task: Set up separate user accounts for children
items.why: Creates isolated environments with appropriate permissions and prevents children from changing security settings.
items.howTo: Create standard (non-administrator) user accounts on computers and tablets. Configure age-appropriate content ratings and app installation restrictions.

items.task: Enable router-level content filtering
items.why: Provides network-wide protection that can't be easily bypassed and protects all connected devices automatically.
items.howTo: Access your router's admin panel and enable content filtering features. Consider upgrading to routers with built-in parental controls or using DNS filtering services like OpenDNS.

items.task: Configure privacy settings on all browsers
items.why: Reduces data collection and tracking while providing additional security against malicious websites.
items.howTo: Disable third-party cookies, enable pop-up blockers, turn on phishing protection, and set browsers to clear data on exit. Consider using a privacy-focused browser for enhanced privacy.

items.task: Install and configure antivirus software
items.why: Protects against malware that could compromise your child's personal information or device security.
items.howTo: Install reputable antivirus software with real-time scanning, web protection, and parental control features. Enable automatic updates and regular system scans.

items.task: Review and restrict social media app installations
items.why: Many social platforms collect extensive personal data and expose children to cyberbullying, inappropriate content, and potential predators.
items.howTo: Use app store restrictions to prevent installation of age-inappropriate social apps. For allowed apps, create accounts together and review privacy settings thoroughly.

items.task: Configure privacy settings on existing social media accounts
items.why: Default settings often share too much personal information publicly, putting children at risk of identity theft and unwanted contact.
items.howTo: Set all profiles to private, disable location sharing, restrict who can contact your child, and turn off data sharing with third parties. Regularly audit these settings.

items.task: Set up friend/contact approval systems
items.why: Prevents unknown individuals from contacting your child and helps you monitor their social interactions online.
items.howTo: Enable friend request notifications, require approval for new contacts, and regularly review your child's friend lists and message history.

items.task: Disable location services for social and gaming apps
items.why: Location data can be used to track your child's movements and may be shared with advertisers or malicious actors.
items.howTo: Go to device privacy settings and disable location access for social media, gaming, and entertainment apps. Only allow location access for essential apps like maps.

items.task: Review and limit in-app purchases and subscriptions
items.why: Prevents unauthorized charges and reduces exposure to manipulative monetization tactics targeting children.
items.howTo: Disable in-app purchases in device settings, remove stored payment methods from app stores, and require password authentication for all purchases.

items.task: Set up content reporting and blocking features
items.why: Provides tools to quickly address cyberbullying, inappropriate content, or suspicious behavior from other users.
items.howTo: Familiarize yourself with reporting mechanisms on each platform, show your child how to block users and report content, and establish clear guidelines for when to seek help.

items.task: Teach children about personal information protection
items.why: Children often don't understand the long-term consequences of sharing personal details online or how this information can be misused.
items.howTo: Explain what constitutes personal information (full name, address, school, phone number). Practice scenarios where they might be asked for this information and appropriate responses.

items.task: Establish clear rules about online interactions
items.why: Predators often build trust gradually before requesting meetings or personal information, making clear guidelines essential for safety.
items.howTo: Create family rules about never meeting online friends in person, not sharing photos, and immediately telling parents about uncomfortable conversations or requests.

items.task: Set up regular monitoring and check-ins
items.why: Consistent oversight helps identify potential problems early and reinforces the importance of online safety rules.
items.howTo: Schedule weekly reviews of browsing history, app usage, and social media activity. Use this time for open discussions about their online experiences.

items.task: Create a family media agreement
items.why: Clear expectations and consequences help children make better decisions and provide a framework for addressing violations.
items.howTo: Draft a written agreement covering screen time limits, acceptable websites and apps, consequences for rule violations, and procedures for reporting problems.

items.task: Teach recognition of phishing and scam attempts
items.why: Children are particularly vulnerable to scams and may unknowingly provide personal information or download malware.
items.howTo: Show examples of common scams targeting children, explain warning signs like urgent requests or too-good-to-be-true offers, and practice identifying suspicious messages.

items.task: Establish screen-free zones and times
items.why: Balanced technology use promotes healthy development and provides regular opportunities for family communication about online experiences.
items.howTo: Designate bedrooms and dining areas as screen-free zones. Implement daily screen-free periods and use parental controls to enforce these boundaries automatically.

items.task: Verify COPPA compliance for all services
items.why: COPPA protects children under 13 from excessive data collection, and non-compliant services may illegally collect your child's personal information.
items.howTo: Check privacy policies for COPPA statements, verify age requirements before signing up for services, and use only platforms that explicitly comply with COPPA regulations.

items.task: Monitor your child's digital footprint
items.why: Information shared online can persist indefinitely and may affect future opportunities or expose children to identity theft risks.
items.howTo: Regularly search for your child's name and images online, set up Google alerts for their full name, and remove inappropriate content when possible.

items.task: Set up credit monitoring for identity theft protection
items.why: Child identity theft is increasingly common and may go undetected for years, causing significant financial and legal problems.
items.howTo: Request credit reports annually, consider freezing your child's credit files, and monitor for signs of identity theft like unexpected mail or account notifications.

items.task: Review and limit data sharing permissions
items.why: Many apps and services share personal data with third parties for advertising and analytics, creating privacy risks for children.
items.howTo: Regularly audit app permissions, opt out of data sharing where possible, and delete accounts for unused services that may retain personal information.

items.task: Document and report violations of children's privacy
items.why: Reporting helps protect not just your child but others, and creates accountability for companies that mishandle children's data.
items.howTo: Keep records of inappropriate content or privacy violations, report issues to platform administrators and relevant authorities like the FTC when necessary.

pro_tips: Use a privacy-focused browser's enhanced privacy features to prevent tracking and data collection when your child needs to research school projects online.
Create a shared family calendar to track when you review and update privacy settings - aim for monthly check-ins to stay current with platform changes.
Consider using a VPN designed for families to add an extra layer of privacy protection, especially when using public Wi-Fi networks.
Set up separate email addresses for your child's online accounts to better monitor and control their digital communications.
Keep devices in common areas rather than bedrooms to naturally encourage more oversight and reduce the risk of inappropriate online activities.
